page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and is equipped with 256 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with the stress-ng multi-core test and PassMark CPU score both placing in the top 25% tier. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, which contribute to top-tier performance in image processing and static web serving throughput, both ranking in the top 10%. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 5112.66 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 197.6 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, memory write speeds for large blocks and single-core stress-ng performance align with average mid-tier expectations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i-flex.16xlarge offers a balanced resource density, leveraging high-speed DDR5 memory and dedicated compute resources without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance and high memory read throughput. Best-fit workloads include static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale language model prompt processing.
